# From making calls to delivering results: Tool interfaces, reliability, and collaboration contracts

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration.md) · English

Updated 2026-11-27 · 55 topic entries / 12 representative comparisons

Toolformer learns when to call, SWE-agent designs action interfaces, and RATED addresses reliability among relevant tools. AutoGen programs messaging, MetaGPT structures role deliverables, and World of SWEcraft checks collective output on hidden downstream dependencies. Any layer can fail; a valid call format is not end-to-end completion.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

!!! note "How to read this card"

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Choosing a tool does not establish that it works

Toolformer filters calls by prediction gains, supplying policy-training signal. SWE-agent organizes executable interfaces and their return formats. RATED separates semantic relevance from recent reliability. Record willingness to call, valid format, actual interface success, and task completion independently. Relevance does not compensate for a broken service, and successful calls do not supply counterfactual rewards for unchosen tools.

Sources: [Toolformer](../../../../agent-research/2302.04761-toolformer/README-en.md) · [SWE-agent](../../../../agent-research/2405.15793-swe-agent/README-en.md) · [RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics](../../../../reproductions/2610.13889-rated/README-en.md)

### Messaging protocols, intermediate artifacts, and ecosystem effects

AutoGen programs who replies and when to continue or stop. MetaGPT further constrains role inputs and outputs with SOP deliverables. World of SWEcraft widens evaluation to long-term maintenance across repositories: package tests can pass while downstream consumers break. These methods address control, information handoff, and external effects respectively. Counts of messages, roles, or artifacts do not replace downstream evidence. Long-lived collaboration needs persistent assets and session budgets rather than an indefinitely growing chat.

Sources: [AutoGen](../../../../agent-research/2308.08155-autogen/README-en.md) · [MetaGPT](../../../../agent-research/2308.00352-metagpt/README-en.md) · [World of SWECraft: Agent Collaboration at Scale via Simulated Software Worlds](../../../../agent-research/2610.24061-world-of-swecraft/README-en.md)

### October 29: New method and source changes

Meta's official retrieval-programs repository is now verifiable, updating RPL's prior open-source record. The main repository is CC-BY-NC4; vendored retrieval and training components retain their licenses. Public code does not make the local typed grammar cover arbitrary Python, cross-turn state, neural retrieval, or RL. No source was copied and the existing L1 evidence did not change.

Sources: [Toolformer](../../../../agent-research/2302.04761-toolformer/README-en.md) · [Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning](../../../../agent-research/2610.24854-rpl/README-en.md)

### Even permitted tools need object and amount constraints

Tool-name or recipient allow-lists miss exfiltration through a legitimate endpoint. RuntimeTickets freezes source-grounded recipient/object/amount obligations and checks each effect with a model-free gate. It still depends on trusted egress and observation coverage. A valid local HMAC prefix is not a complete sealed/closed account, and at-most-once callback invocation is not network exactly-once delivery.

Sources: [RuntimeTickets: Source-Grounded Security Obligations for Agent Skills](../../../../agent-research/2611.03772-runtime-tickets/README-en.md) · [Toolformer](../../../../agent-research/2302.04761-toolformer/README-en.md) · [SWE-agent](../../../../agent-research/2405.15793-swe-agent/README-en.md)

### Learning when to call a tool and dispatching in code are different deliverables

Toolformer filters calls by the help their real results provide to downstream token loss and continues model training. ReTrace recovers conditions from SOPs and reasoning, compiling runtime choice into code. The former retains model-generation control; the latter still permits models inside fixed tools. Tool-call counts alone cannot rank them: local Toolformer uses deterministic utility rather than GPT-J loss, and local ReTrace is only typed IR. Neither supplies complete original-model or production evidence.

Sources: [ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows](../../../../agent-research/2611.14492-retrace/README-en.md) · [Toolformer](../../../../agent-research/2302.04761-toolformer/README-en.md)

### Pre-effect checks must expose the origin of their authority

CapLite removes model-written security policy in favor of trusted schemas, request grounding and write commitments. RuntimeTickets allows proposed obligations but freezes source-backed host-approved tickets before checking objects and budgets. Neither permits untrusted observations to authorize effects or protects tools that bypass mediation. Security is more than an allow flag.

Sources: [CapLite: Prompt-Injection Defense for Small Language Model Agents without Model-Written Security Artifacts](../../../../agent-research/2611.17115-caplite/README-en.md) · [RuntimeTickets: Source-Grounded Security Obligations for Agent Skills](../../../../agent-research/2611.03772-runtime-tickets/README-en.md)

### Subgraph recovery versus effect protection: preserved state is not unique effects

SGR preserves states and outputs outside the failed node and its descendants. Detection and budget decisions are external; DSP first cascades unreachable, and the caller decides whether to retry. Children require every parent complete and inherit actual outputs in declared order. Prompt mutation is a preliminary appendix probe, not the shipped core loop. Local transactional claims and generation/owner checks reject late pre-reopen output under explicit single-scheduler handover, not a distributed lease proof. Character admission is not model-token budgeting. An exception-after-mutation control deliberately produces two mutations, preserving the absence of exactly-once guarantees. Three seeds with four nodes/five calls test scope, sibling preservation and text dependencies, not agent capability, semantic correction or paper latency gains.

Sources: [fork() for Agents: Agent Kernel for Non-blocking LLM Orchestration](../../../../agent-research/2611.31727-agent-kernel/README-en.md) · [RuntimeTickets: Source-Grounded Security Obligations for Agent Skills](../../../../agent-research/2611.03772-runtime-tickets/README-en.md)

### Local-closure certificates do not permit reading hidden deployment configurations

Calibration can query candidate h in a reproducible test environment for f(a,h)=(observation,commit). Returned policies contain actions/response branches only; deployment receives tool observations. Closed actions compose successes by union and call mass by |V| plus child mass. Unknown programs optimistically commit; unknown probes optimistically separate each configuration. Selected T2 tightens only the current action's two-call continuations. Witnesses preserve R0 and remain executable under consistent added effects; valid equal root bounds certify optimality. The local slice supports one to eight configurations and one to four calls with query-count rather than wall-clock allowance. Its four-configuration diagnostic acquires all twenty cells and saves no calibration. The independent oracle stays evaluator-side. Random finite tables, interrupted coverage, bounds and outside-scope-unknown controls establish neither native CSV/JSON behavior nor LLM success gains.

Sources: [CAPE: Coordinating Calibration and Search for Tool-Use Policies](../../../../agent-research/2611.31938-cape/README-en.md) · [CapLite: Prompt-Injection Defense for Small Language Model Agents without Model-Written Security Artifacts](../../../../agent-research/2611.17115-caplite/README-en.md)

### Authenticated origins do not replace semantic authorization or effect contracts

Separate agent summaries from authenticated authorizer input. Occurrence MACs, ordered commitments and current-count/fresh-boundary checks jointly close echo, replay and omission gaps. Persistent-counter tests assume protected keys/state/issuance; SQLite is not agent isolation. RuntimeTickets freezes host-restricting effect contracts, audits before callbacks and avoids retries under uncertainty, but its local chain does not prove complete prefixes. The layers compose without local LLM attack-rate evidence. The full multi-model/live matrix is terminally not reproduced for cost.

Sources: [LLM Agent Authorization Across Context Compaction](../../../../agent-research/2611.32194-compaction-authorization/README-en.md) · [RuntimeTickets: Source-Grounded Security Obligations for Agent Skills](../../../../agent-research/2611.03772-runtime-tickets/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### Why might RATED deprioritize a tool whose API call Toolformer selected as useful? {#cross-usefulness-versus-reliability}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Training selection shows that returned values helped prediction, not continued service availability or stable argument behavior. RATED first restricts to relevant tools, then updates reliability from selected tools' actual successes, errors, and timeouts using discounting. Training usefulness and current executability are separate, and one failure cannot assign negative rewards to all untried tools.

    **Illustrative example:** An exchange-rate API can help training and time out repeatedly in deployment. It remains relevant, but actual reliability should affect future choices.

    Sources: [Toolformer](../../../../agent-research/2302.04761-toolformer/README-en.md) · [RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics](../../../../reproductions/2610.13889-rated/README-en.md)

### If AutoGen already has programmer and tester roles, why do MetaGPT and SWE-agent emphasize structured deliverables and ACI? {#cross-message-protocol-versus-artifact}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Role names specify responsibilities, while AutoGen's replies and stopping organize interaction. MetaGPT specifies deliverables for requirements, design, and implementation to reduce drift in free chat. SWE-agent defines concrete viewing, editing, and testing actions. Control, information contracts, and action interfaces are complementary, not interchangeable.

    **Illustrative example:** A tester can know when to reply without a clear interface specification. Even with a complete spec, an imprecise editing command can change the wrong code.

    Sources: [AutoGen](../../../../agent-research/2308.08155-autogen/README-en.md) · [MetaGPT](../../../../agent-research/2308.00352-metagpt/README-en.md) · [SWE-agent](../../../../agent-research/2405.15793-swe-agent/README-en.md)

### Why does World of SWEcraft use hidden downstream packages after MetaGPT or SWE-agent repository tests pass? {#cross-local-tests-versus-downstream}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Own tests cover maintainer-visible contracts and may only improve visible microbenchmarks. API changes can break real consumers. Hidden downstream checks install frozen release versions to assess collective delivery. Retain failed packages in speed accounting and declare strict/carry semantics. A local micro pass does not establish ecosystem capability.

    **Illustrative example:** Renaming an argument and updating library tests can still break consumers using the old name; downstream checks reveal it.

    Sources: [MetaGPT](../../../../agent-research/2308.00352-metagpt/README-en.md) · [SWE-agent](../../../../agent-research/2405.15793-swe-agent/README-en.md) · [World of SWECraft: Agent Collaboration at Scale via Simulated Software Worlds](../../../../agent-research/2610.24061-world-of-swecraft/README-en.md)

### Why retain local RPL component limitations after finding the official repository? {#cross-oct29-method-boundary}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Source completeness and execution fidelity are different. Published training code does not make the existing constrained SDK execute the full policy, neural retrieval, or distillation. Future integration needs separate cost, execution, and license checks.

    **Illustrative example:** Learning the official training entry point does not turn local retrieval-program syntax tests into multi-hop QA evaluation.

    Sources: [Toolformer](../../../../agent-research/2302.04761-toolformer/README-en.md) · [Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning](../../../../agent-research/2610.24854-rpl/README-en.md)

### If both systems emit the same query call, how do Toolformer training and ReTrace workflow dispatch differ? {#cross-compiled-rule-versus-learned-call}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Inspect how the call is produced and what supports it. Toolformer training changes model call-generation probabilities. ReTrace tests available guards, selects the first match and binds sourced arguments. Matching one output establishes neither training nor compilation fidelity and cannot let future tool results fill missing observations.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: one order query comes from a model prediction and another from a code condition saying no query has occurred. Identical calls do not establish equivalent exception handling.

    Sources: [ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows](../../../../agent-research/2611.14492-retrace/README-en.md) · [Toolformer](../../../../agent-research/2302.04761-toolformer/README-en.md)

### Can grounded CapLite arguments replace RuntimeTickets cumulative limits? {#cross-cross-nov15-caplite}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Grounding says values occur in the request, not how many times or bytes legal actions may accumulate. Separate grant/budget and replay contracts are required.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: one authorized email does not authorize a thousand repeated deliveries.

    Sources: [CapLite: Prompt-Injection Defense for Small Language Model Agents without Model-Written Security Artifacts](../../../../agent-research/2611.17115-caplite/README-en.md) · [RuntimeTickets: Source-Grounded Security Obligations for Agent Skills](../../../../agent-research/2611.03772-runtime-tickets/README-en.md)

### Can SGR state preservation replace RuntimeTickets? {#cross-cross-nov25-agent-kernel}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. SGR preserves sibling SAB records and permits reexecution. RuntimeTickets checks authority and obligations before effects and avoids automatic resend under callback uncertainty. Recovery and effect authorization are separate layers.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: a payment succeeds before its node throws, so SGR may run it again. An effect-layer transaction/idempotency contract is needed; unchanged siblings do not prevent duplicate payment.

    Sources: [fork() for Agents: Agent Kernel for Non-blocking LLM Orchestration](../../../../agent-research/2611.31727-agent-kernel/README-en.md) · [RuntimeTickets: Source-Grounded Security Obligations for Agent Skills](../../../../agent-research/2611.03772-runtime-tickets/README-en.md)

### Does protected CAPE coverage imply CapLite-style safety? {#cross-cross-nov25-cape}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. CAPE maximizes completion over parser candidates, then minimizes calls. CapLite freezes trusted write order and authority grounding. Matching a reference does not establish user authorization or write-prefix safety.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: an upload may commit under all four date parsers while sending the correct data to an unauthorized recipient.

    Sources: [CAPE: Coordinating Calibration and Search for Tool-Use Policies](../../../../agent-research/2611.31938-cape/README-en.md) · [CapLite: Prompt-Injection Defense for Small Language Model Agents without Model-Written Security Artifacts](../../../../agent-research/2611.17115-caplite/README-en.md)

### Does this gate protect the same boundary as RuntimeTickets? {#cross-cross-nov27-compaction-authorization}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. It protects authorization input before policy synthesis; RuntimeTickets checks frozen recipient/object/budget contracts before effects. Intact originals do not prove correct policy semantics or authenticate summaries through valid sends.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: a generator can still broaden recipients after reading authentic text, requiring effect-level ticket checks rather than treating MACs as semantic understanding.

    Sources: [LLM Agent Authorization Across Context Compaction](../../../../agent-research/2611.32194-compaction-authorization/README-en.md) · [RuntimeTickets: Source-Grounded Security Obligations for Agent Skills](../../../../agent-research/2611.03772-runtime-tickets/README-en.md)
